title: De Incarnatione Et Gratia
author: Petrus Diaconus of Monte Cassino
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0227b.stoa002.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: Propterea etiam essentialem, sive naturalem factam naturarum unitionem omnimodis confitemur; n< n sicut illi, qui tanquam in propheta, ita in Christo b Deum Verbum inoperasse contendunt. Quos redarguit beatus Gregorius, Nazianzenus ad Clidonium, dicens : c Si quis sicut in propheta secundum gratiam dicit inoperasse Deum Verbum, et non esseniialiter factam confitetur unitionem, sit vacuus melioris inoperationis, magis autem plenus sit detenoris. » Nec sicut illi qui secundum illustrationem, aut dilectionem aut affectionem, personalem vel subsistentialem, sive secundum auctoritatem, aut potentiam, aut aequalitatem honoris, unitionem tentant astruere naturarum.
passages.english: For this reason also we confess in every way that the union of the natures came about essentially, or naturally; not as those do who contend that God the Word worked in Christ as [he worked] in a prophet. These the blessed Gregory of Nazianzus refutes, [writing] to Cledonius, saying: "If anyone says that God the Word worked [in him] by grace, as in a prophet, and does not confess that the union came about essentially, let him be empty of the better working, and rather let him be full of the worse." Nor [do we confess it] as those do who try to establish a personal or subsistential union of the natures according to illumination, or love, or affection, or according to authority, or power, or equality of honour.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected silently: "n< n" read as "non", "esseniialiter" as "essentialiter", "detenoris" as "deterioris"; stray letters "b" and "c" are footnote marks. The Latin "inoperasse" renders Greek energein, 'to work in'. The phrase "personalem vel subsistentialem" may modify "affectionem" rather than "unitionem" ('personal or subsistential affection'); it is taken here with "unitionem".
